name: upwell_config
doc: Configuration for the Upwell framework.
docs:
Configuration for the Upwell framework.

Two layers live here. The **parser** is the format-agnostic core: a normalized
[`ConfigValue`] tree, a placeholder grammar (`${KEY}` / `${KEY:default}`), a
[`Resolver`] chain, and a custom [`from_value`] deserializer that resolves placeholders
*while* deserializing. The **managed** layer (this crate's `managed` module) integrates
that parser with dependency injection: [`Cfg<T>`] injectables, the [`ConfigManager`]
that loads and merges files, the [`ConfigStore`] resolver the DI container reaches
config through, and the two-phase [`ConfigReloader`].

The parser's substitution failure type is [`TemplateError`]; the managed layer's
load/bind failure type is [`ConfigError`].

name: condition
doc: Raw config reads for component conditions.
docs:
Raw config reads for component conditions.

A condition may read a config path that no type binds through [`resolve`]. The
application resolves every declared raw path of the candidate config into a
[`ResolvedConfig`] before evaluation, so callbacks never touch resolvers or ambient
process state themselves.

name: resolve
signature: pub fn resolve<T: DeserializeOwned>(path: &'static str) -> Option<T>
doc: Reads the config value at path inside a component condition.
docs:
Reads the config value at `path` inside a component condition.

`path` must be a string literal so the condition declares it statically. A missing key
answers `None`. A present value that does not deserialize into `T` fails the condition
evaluation, as does reading a path the condition did not declare; both also answer
`None` so the expression can finish. The value deserializes with the ordinary config
deserializer, so it coerces exactly like a `#[config]` field.

The deserialization error itself is dropped: it can quote the config value, and
condition diagnostics are redacted to the path and target type.

# Panics

Panics when called outside a condition evaluation.

name: ResolvedConfig
doc: A config subtree with every placeholder rendered, as supplied to condition callbacks.
docs:
A config subtree with every placeholder rendered, as supplied to condition callbacks.

Rendering keeps templated strings templated and turns literals and full placeholders into
literals, which both coerce from their rendered text, so deserializing a resolved subtree
coerces exactly like deserializing the source subtree. Values compare structurally,
which is how an unchanged raw input is recognised across reloads.

name: from_value
signature: pub fn from_value<T: DeserializeOwned>(root: &upwell_config::value::ConfigValue, resolvers: &upwell_config::resolve::ResolverChain) -> Result<T, upwell_config::error::TemplateError>
doc: Deserializes T from a ConfigValue tree, resolving placeholders through the resolver chain.
docs:
Deserializes `T` from a [`ConfigValue`] tree, resolving placeholders through the
resolver chain.

Pure and re-runnable: it performs no I/O beyond what the resolvers do and never
mutates the tree, so a hot-reload is simply "build a fresh tree and call this
again".

name: from_value_in
signature: pub fn from_value_in<T: DeserializeOwned>(root: &upwell_config::value::ConfigValue, value: &upwell_config::value::ConfigValue, resolvers: &upwell_config::resolve::ResolverChain) -> Result<T, upwell_config::error::TemplateError>
doc: Like from_value, but deserializes value (typically a subtree) while resolving placeholders against root (the full tree).
docs:
Like [`from_value`], but deserializes `value` (typically a subtree) while
resolving placeholders against `root` (the full tree).

Property-path placeholders such as `${app.server.port}` are absolute paths from
the root, so deserializing the `app.server` subtree must still resolve them
against the whole config — not the subtree, where that path does not exist.

name: ValueDeserializer
doc: A serde Deserializer over a single ConfigValue node.
docs:
A serde `Deserializer` over a single `ConfigValue` node.

Scalar coercion is chosen by *which* `deserialize_*` method the target type calls:
a full `${...}` placeholder defers its type to that method, while a templated leaf
can only ever satisfy `deserialize_str`. The `path` is carried purely for error
context.

name: DefaultSpec
doc: The shape of a config type's field defaults, emitted by the #config macro and consumed by the merge step.
docs:
The shape of a config type's field defaults, emitted by the `#[config]` macro and
consumed by the merge step.

Built from `&'static` data so it is `Copy` and `const`-constructible: the macro emits it as
an associated const ([`ConfigProperties::DEFAULTS`](../../upwell_core/config/trait.ConfigProperties.html)).
Struct defaults fill every missing field; enum defaults fill only the fields of the variant
actually present in the config, since variants are mutually exclusive and a phantom variant
branch would confuse the deserializer. An enum may also name a **default variant**
(`#[default]` on a variant), used when the config selects none.

name: fill_missing
signature: pub fn fill_missing(&self, subtree: &mut ConfigValue) -> Result<(), TemplateError>
doc: Fills missing leaves of subtree in place from these defaults. Existing values are never overwritten; only absent fields are added.
docs:
Fills missing leaves of `subtree` in place from these defaults. Existing values are
never overwritten; only absent fields are added.

For [`Fields`](DefaultSpec::Fields) the subtree is treated as a table and every
missing field is filled. For [`Variants`](DefaultSpec::Variants) only the fields of
the variant present in the config are filled; when no variant is present the
`#[default]` variant (if any) is synthesized in the enum's tagged shape.

An injected configuration value, bound from a property path.

Backed by a shared [`Live<T>`] slot, so a config reload swaps the value in place
and every holder observes it on the next read; snapshots taken earlier stay
pinned. The path is supplied at the injection site via `#[config("...")]` (or
omitted for the sole-binding shorthand). Read with [`get`](Self::get) (a guard)
or [`snapshot`](Self::snapshot) (an owned `Arc`).

Runtime, object-safe access to a config type's [`DefaultSpec`].

[`ConfigProperties`] exposes its defaults as the associated `const`

`const` is not part of the vtable). This companion trait — blanket-implemented for every

read from a value or a `dyn ConfigDefaults`.

name: ConfigOverlay
doc: Property assignments merged above every config source, so a proposed change can be staged without editing a source file.
docs:
Property assignments merged above every config source, so a proposed change can be
staged without editing a source file.

Each assignment replaces the node at its dotted path; later assignments win. Values are
scalar literals: `true`/`false`, integers (`i128`), finite floats, `"quoted strings"`, and
otherwise the bare text as a string. A number outside those ranges is rejected rather than
converted. String values keep `${…}` placeholders, exactly as a source file
would. Overlays are ordinary config sources: bound defaults still fill missing leaves
underneath them.

doc: The config staging engine one application runtime drives.
docs:
The config staging engine one application runtime drives.

It owns the managed config tree and the reloadable slots of every bound config, and
serializes reloads. It does not publish on its own: the application runtime's
transactional reload stages through it, prepares and validates a candidate
generation, and commits the staged values at its terminal publication. Request a
reload through the application's runtime reloader, not through this handle.

doc: Stages a reload without committing anything: re-reads the sources, diffs each binding's subtree, and deserializes changed bindings into committable swaps.
docs:
Stages a reload without committing anything: re-reads the sources, diffs each
binding's subtree, and deserializes changed bindings into committable swaps.

The returned [`StagedReload`] is inert until [`StagedReload::commit`] is called,
so a caller can run its own validation, hooks, or graph preparation between the
two — over [`StagedReload::candidate_store`], which lazily re-seeds every
binding into fresh cells without touching the active ones. The caller is
responsible for serializing stage → commit against other reloads by holding
[`lock_reload`](Self::lock_reload) across the whole transaction.

Fires the config-reload event against `hooks` for every hook that targets a changed
binding (or is routed `always`), returning the accepted participant outcomes in
registration order. Participants run sequentially and the first error aborts the
whole reload with [`ConfigReloadError::Hook`]; later participants and observers do
not run. Observers run once every participant accepted, and their failures are
logged without affecting the reload.

`owner_id` names the component owning each hook: reports and errors carry the ID it
returns for the hook's owner type, so the caller decides the naming scheme.

The application runtime's transactional reload runs it against the candidate
generation's manager before commit, naming owners by their stable component IDs.

Implemented for the std scalars and collections and, by `#[config]`, for every config type,

to tracing their `Deserialize` impl.

name: Probe
doc: A zero-sized stand-in for a field type, probed by method resolution.
docs:
A zero-sized stand-in for a field type, probed by method resolution.

`(&&&Probe::<T>::NEW).value_schema()` resolves to the most specific applicable level:
[`ViaDescribed`] (`T: DescribedValue`), then [`ViaSerde`] (`T: DeserializeOwned`, traced),
then [`ViaOpaque`] (any `T`). Autoref ranking happens at the macro's concrete field type, so
no specialization is needed and an undescribable field type still compiles.

name: ConfigValue
doc: A format-agnostic configuration value tree.
docs:
A format-agnostic configuration value tree.

Every source format (TOML, YAML, ...) normalizes into this type, so placeholder
parsing, resolution, and the typed deserializer are written exactly once. String
leaves are pre-parsed into placeholder segments at construction time, which keeps
(re-)deserialization allocation-light and side-effect-free — the property a future
hot-reload relies on.

name: get_path

docs:

An empty path returns the root. `None` if any segment is missing or traverses
a non-table.

docs:
Builds a string leaf by parsing `raw` for `${...}` placeholders — the inverse of
rendering. Used to inject default values into the tree so a templated default such
as `${tcp.ip}:${tcp.port}` resolves through the same pipeline as a file value.
Errors only on a structurally invalid template (an unterminated `${`).
